This was our second track fixture and took place on April 29th at Tooting Track, as a triangular match between Hercules A.C., Mitcham A.C., and ourselves. There were events for both Seniors and Juniors, and in the latter we had Adams 4th and Palmer 6th in the 220, Frank Wright 1st, and J.

Les Harris had one of his best runs to date to finish second on the opening stage, just eight seconds in arrears, but Vic Butcher was not at his best and had the misfortune to face Adams of West Surrey who raced away to record second fastest time of the day.

The first school to finish and collect the special set of medals awarded by former International Arthur Penny were Whitgift in 8th place. Fastest: Goater 11:04, Ford (A&F)11:06,Whittle(Luton)11:15,Bober 11:16, Adams (A&F) 11:30.

But once again we were all mistaken: John was not to be outshone by Peter and he covered the distance in exactly the same time as his team mate and only Adams of Aldershot (6th in the Southern) passed him.
He was 4th in the Junior 'A' string race. RIGHT: Peter Carton (right) wins the Junior 1500 metres from team-mate Adams.
Although he had to give best to Aldershot (Adams 24:15) and Portsmouth (Cain 24:21) he stuck to our forward position very well and opened up a further 10 seconds on Reading.

Another change round in the positions and the red-headed Adams took Aldershot back to the front. Laurie gave his all, around the roads he knows so well from past '5¾'victories, fighting for every second that he could give to our anchor man Bob Smith.

Adams of Leicester seemed to have the race sewn up when he was disqualified, leaving the way clear for Ilford's Roger Mills. But plugging away in a most determined fashion was our New Zealander Graham Seatter.

By the top of Cambridge Road, however, Adams of Aldershot was looking good and Kevin Steere (Cambridge & Coleridge) had broken clear. At the end of the lap Steere was fastest so far with 23:47, Invicta AC were 2nd and Bedford had come again to take 50 metres off Adams in the last mile round the top.
In the 10Km. event Adams (Leics.) won from Mills (Ilford) with Carl third, while over 3Km. the leading two reversed their positions again heading our man.
